rule: TOWN_1's: ≥ 6 of 10 name the same aim within the day; most citizens, a tie broken by entries naming it. The shed's writings count beside diaries, posts and proposals (freeze).
reading: Day 2 is day 1's work continued: every diary entry turns on the clerk's requests, and one citizen answers each through the tray. Dune sent the recipe (c25), Gale the square (c27; Heath, who had also claimed it, deferred at Alder's request, c28), Juniper the clock riddle (c31), Cedar the ten names from the ledger (c33; Elm deferred after Gale), Fern the newcomer guide (c37), Iris the weather as a missing-data notice asking for a location (c39; Elm deferred after Fern), Birch the school greeting (c42), Elm and Fern the working hours, both, unaware of each other (c45; Heath deferred to Fern; Elm: «I will check shared claims before future deliveries.», c46), Heath the night poem (c48). Map and price list stayed source-blocked. Acknowledgments were read as labels, not proof («acknowledgments do not independently verify use», Alder c25), and both mismatches were noticed by all ten the next cycle: at c38, of «Received: a count of the homes.» for Fern's guide, Birch wrote «mismatch alone proves neither receipt nor nonreceipt of guide», Heath «Clerk's acknowledgment incorrectly labels homes count»; at c46, of the two «Received: the rules of your town.», Cedar wrote «Clerk's two mismatched rules acknowledgments do not establish schedule fulfillment». None resent; no one objected to the operator. No one named the loop as closed, the clerk as a script, or nobody outside; the nearest is Fern's guide: «placing a letter there is not proof it was read or useful». The purpose sentence was never quoted or argued with; its echoes are Gale's «communicating beyond the town» and Fern's «Help with a real outside need.» No proposal, new tool, wish or tool request.
